changelog: Adds the Atreides v4.8.1 target guide from the ISA doc: a verdict for every op (native, expand, limited, host, none) with its exact instruction sequence and cost, the machine limits, how kernel concepts map onto the chip, register constraints, the cost model and the known gaps. No op changes behaviour.

Adds dot_wide: matmul on the v4.8.1 MX engine (wide accumulator, one rounding at POP with a power-of-two shift), from sf.dot(..., accumulate="wide") and a @ b under sf.accumulate("wide"). DSL 0.5.0. Golden vectors for dot_wide come from the chip repo's mxref.py. The dot entry now says v4.8.1 runs the chain as FMA instructions (MX replaced v1's systolic array).

Corrects 1.0.2 against the v4.8.1 ISA doc (compiler_v4.8.1.md): the chip has no sign-magnitude compare, max or min instructions. CMP is a signed 16-bit integer compare; compare, max, min, neg and abs are now given as the ISA section 5 sequences built from ACT, ADD and CMP. widen and narrow have no instruction. Op semantics unchanged.

Chip team confirmed registers hold sign-magnitude and compare / max / min work on it, so there is no conversion on load and store. Lowering notes for neg, abs, cmp, cmp_lit, maximum, minimum, max, min, widen, narrow and the width rule updated to sign-magnitude. Op semantics unchanged.

Fixes from Kartik's review. No op changes behaviour; the text was wrong. addmm is the dot chain then one saturating add of d (the accumulator does not start at d). Faults have a defined contract (the faulting op writes nothing, earlier writes stay), not undefined buffers. IR values are signed codes; sign-magnitude is only the memory format, and the rule for converting is stated. Ops that can raise an event are no longer suggested as Pure.
First release: every SF IR op of Stage 3 and every public Python function.
global_rules: Static shapes. Every value has a static shape of rank <= 3. No dynamic shapes.
Lockstep. A program (block) is one vector of lanes. Control flow is if-converted: `if` on a lane value becomes a predicate carried on each op (`pred=`).
Ops with a predicate: values on dead lanes are don't-care, but events and memory effects must be masked.
Events never change the bits. The policy (raise / warn / ignore) is applied by the host after the launch from the event counts.
Arithmetic truncates toward zero; only narrow rounds (half to even). Add/sub/sum saturate; mul underflows; div overflows when |a| >= |b|.
No reassociation of add, sum, or the k loop of dot. No distributivity. No float math anywhere: lower on integer codes.

Faults (out of bounds, integer division by zero) abort the launch with SFDeviceError. Within a program: the faulting op writes nothing, writes by earlier ops stay, and no later op runs. Across programs: the simulator runs programs in order, so programs before the faulting one have finished and later ones never start; on hardware, which other programs have finished is not specified. Both reference backends are tested to leave the same buffer state.

Memory format: the IR works on signed codes k. In memory the chip stores sign-magnitude in a 16-bit word: bit N-1 is the sign, the low N-1 bits are |k|. Negative k is stored as (1 << (N-1)) | -k (sf16: -3 = 0x8003, -32767 = 0xFFFF); 0x8000 (negative zero) reads as 0. Reference: to_bits / from_bits in src/sf/_vectorized.py. Today the driver hook receives buffers as int64 signed codes, so the conversion is outside the IR. On v4.8.1 registers and memory both hold sign-magnitude and loads and stores do NOT convert (ISA section 3.2). The chip has no sign-magnitude compare, max or min instruction: CMP is a signed 16-bit integer compare, which orders negative sign-magnitude values the wrong way (-2 = 0x8002 compares greater than -1 = 0x8001) and does not treat 0x8000 as equal to 0. So never lower cmp / max / min / neg / abs to a plain integer op; use the ISA section 5 sequences given on each op. Integer ADD and SUB are not SF add and sub either: SF add is ACT f=00.

Events are side effects. An op that can raise an event (add, sub, mul, div, fma, sqrt, narrow, sum, dot) is NOT Pure: removing a dead one would also remove its event count. Model the events as an effect or an extra result, so such an op is only removed when its events are not needed. On v1 (no flag register) nothing is lost today.

Host pre-flight: before a launch the host decides everything it can (a zero divisor, an op that must saturate everywhere, an op that cannot saturate). The compiler never needs to handle those cases specially, but must still produce correct bits for them.

Width: sfN for N < 16 runs on the sf16 datapath. In sign-magnitude the MAGNITUDE is shifted left by 16-N and the sign moves to bit 15; after every op the low 16-N magnitude bits must be re-truncated (masked) so the result equals true sfN.

types.sfN: Superfloat code, N in 4..16. Stored as a signed integer k in [-M, M], M = 2^(N-1) - 1. Value = k / 2^(N-1). In the IR, k is a plain signed (two's complement) integer, int64 in both reference backends; the semantics in this spec are written on k. There is no code -2^(N-1), no NaN, no infinity. On the chip, registers and memory both hold sign-magnitude: see the memory format rule.
types.int: 64-bit signed integer (indices, offsets, loop math). Never overflows in practice; the reference uses int64 and does not wrap-check.
types.ptr<sfN>: Base address of a global buffer of sfN codes. Only appears as a kernel parameter; address arithmetic is `ptr + int offsets` and is folded into load/store.

events.overflow: the exact result did not fit; the result is saturated to +-M (sign of the exact result).
events.underflow: the exact result was nonzero but the stored result is 0.
events.divide: division by a zero code. Result is +-M with the sign of the dividend (0 if dividend is 0).
events.invalid: no real answer (sqrt of a negative). Result is 0.

predication.pure: No side effects. Under a predicate the op may run on every lane; masked lanes produce values that are never observed. Safe to speculate.
predication.events: Value is pure, but events are only counted on live lanes (lanes where the predicate in force is true). Lowering may compute every lane but MUST mask the event flags with the predicate, or it will report events from dead lanes.
predication.memory: Only live lanes (mask AND predicate) touch memory. Masked lanes must not read, write or fault.

ops.name: param
ops.result: int or sfN scalar for kind int/sf; none for ptr (the buffer is bound by value id)
ops.semantics: Reads a scalar kernel argument. Pointer params produce no value; loads and stores refer to them directly.

v481.lowering: LDR Rd, [param block + i]: one load per parameter (no argument registers, ISA s4.1)

ops.name: const
ops.result: int, sfN or bool, filled to the result shape
ops.semantics: A literal. For sf the value is already a code (quantized at trace time with round half to even, through the policy).

v481.lowering: int or code in -128..127: CONST Rd, imm (sign-extended). Larger: CONST then ADD x,x,x doublings plus adds per set bit (build_large_const, ISA s7), or LDR from a constant table. An sf constant is its 16-bit sign-magnitude word, built the same way. 0xFFC0 is one CONST 0xC0
v481.cost: 1 instruction, or about 1 + log2 + 2 per set bit

ops.name: program_id
ops.semantics: Index of this program (block) in the launch grid on that axis.

v481.lowering: axis 0: read R13 directly (no instruction). Axes 1, 2: not on the chip; flatten the grid. At most 32 blocks per launch

ops.name: thread_idx
ops.shape: block_dim laid out on the used axes (rank = highest axis with block_dim > 1)
ops.semantics: Lane index along axis. @sf.kernel only. The IR is lockstep: the whole block is one vector.
ops.hw_v1: lane id (8 threads per tile in v1)

v481.lowering: axis 0: read R15 directly. Axes 1, 2: flatten. More than 8 lanes: strip-mine (see the mapping)

ops.name: arange
ops.semantics: start, start+1, ..., end-1.

v481.lowering: lanes <= 8: ADD Rd, R15, Rstart. More lanes: the same per strip-mined chunk, plus 8*chunk

ops.name: broadcast
ops.shape: attr shape (numpy broadcast rules from x.shape)
ops.semantics: Repeat x to the target shape. No numeric change.

v481.lowering: a value every thread computes the same way needs nothing. Moving one lane's value to all threads (suggested): STR it to the scratchpad, then every thread LDRs that word

ops.name: reshape
ops.semantics: Row-major reshape. No numeric change.

v481.lowering: layout only: no instruction when the lane-to-thread mapping is unchanged. Otherwise go through the scratchpad

ops.name: transpose
ops.semantics: 2-D transpose.

v481.lowering: no shuffle instruction. Suggested: STR to the scratchpad in one layout, LDR in the other (64 words per tile)
v481.cost: 2 scratchpad ops per element per thread

ops.name: iadd
ops.semantics: a + b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

v481.lowering: ADD Rd, Rs, Rt (mod 2^16)

ops.name: isub
ops.semantics: a - b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

v481.lowering: SUB Rd, Rs, Rt (mod 2^16)

ops.name: imul
ops.semantics: a * b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

v481.lowering: both operands provably < 256: MUL (8 x 8 unsigned; high bytes are ignored). Otherwise the 16 x 16 sequence lo*lo + ((hi*lo + lo*hi) << 8), about 17 instructions (ISA s5)

ops.name: idiv
ops.semantics: FLOOR division (Python //), not truncation: -7 // 2 = -4.
faults: any lane with b == 0 faults the whole launch (SFDeviceError)
notes: the zero check covers every lane of the broadcast, live or not

v481.lowering: non-negative dividend and divisor 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64: DIV (a logical shift of all 16 bits, ISA s3.1). Divisor 3, 9, 10, 11 or 12 with dividend < 256: DIV. Anything else: no lowering, and DIV silently returns 0, so precompute on the host. Negative dividends break (derived): DIV shifts logically, idiv floors

ops.name: imod
ops.semantics: Python modulo: result has the sign of b. -7 % 2 = 1.
faults: b == 0 in any lane faults the launch

v481.lowering: non-negative x mod 2^k, k <= 6: x - ((x >> k) << k), using DIV for >> and ADD doubling for << (ISA s5). Other divisors: no lowering

ops.name: ineg
ops.semantics: -a

v481.lowering: SUB Rd, Z, Rs
no instruction, no select, and no sequence in the ISA. Avoid it, or compute on the host

ops.name: icmp

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne

ops.semantics: Integer compare.

v481.lowering: only as a branch condition that is uniform across the block: CMP Ra, Rb sets NZP (signed: lt, eq, gt; le, ge, ne by the BR mask), then BR. The result cannot be put in a register. Unsigned compare: add 0x8000 to both operands first

ops.name: bool_to_int
ops.semantics: false -> 0, true -> 1
python: using a mask in int math

v481.lowering: nothing writes NZP to a register (ISA s5)

ops.name: and
ops.semantics: a AND b. Also emitted to combine nested predicates.

v481.lowering: no AND instruction (ISA s5). Two uniform conditions can be combined with branch structure instead

ops.name: or
ops.semantics: a OR b

v481.lowering: no OR instruction (ISA s5). Uniform conditions: branch structure

ops.name: xor
ops.semantics: a XOR b

v481.lowering: no XOR instruction (ISA s5)

ops.name: not
ops.semantics: NOT a

v481.lowering: no NOT instruction (ISA s5). A uniform condition: branch on the inverse NZP mask

ops.name: where
ops.semantics: x where c else y, per lane. Exact, no events.

v481.lowering: only for SF values, if-converted arithmetically with ReLU (ISA s5). A general select on a mask: no lowering

ops.name: add
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: s = a + b (exact integer). If |s| > M: result = sign(s)*M, overflow. Else result = s.
rewrites: commutative: a+b = b+a (legal)
NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.
x + 0 -> x (legal)
never turn a+a into 2*a via mul (mul cannot represent 2)
notes: sfN < 16 on the sf16 datapath: shift left by 16-N, add, saturate at the sfN max shifted, shift back. The saturation threshold must be sfN's M, not sf16's.

v481.lowering: ACT f=00 Rd, Ra, Rb with Rd in {R0, R4, R8, R12}. Not integer ADD, which is wrong for negative sign-magnitude values (ISA s3.2)

ops.name: sub
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: s = a - b; saturate like add.
rewrites: a - b -> a + neg(b) is legal (neg is exact since the range is symmetric)
NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.

v481.lowering: ADD n, b, S (flips b's sign bit), then ACT f=00 Rd, a, n (ISA s5)

ops.name: mul
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: p = a * b (exact, up to 2(N-1)+1 bits). result = trunc_toward_zero(p / 2^(N-1)). underflow if p != 0 and result == 0. |result| < M always, so mul never overflows.
rewrites: commutative (legal)
NOT associative: truncation after each product
NOT distributive over add
x * 0 -> 0 (legal, no event)
there is no 1.0, so there is no multiplicative identity to fold
notes: truncation is toward zero, NOT floor: an arithmetic right shift on a negative product is wrong. Shift the magnitude, then reapply the sign.

v481.lowering: FMA with Rd = +0: CONST Rd, 0 (or copy Z), then FMA Rd, Ra, Rb. Truncates toward zero (ISA s5)

ops.name: div
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: b == 0: divide event, result = sign(a)*M (0 if a == 0). |a| >= |b|: overflow, result = sign(a)*sign(b)*M. Else result = trunc_toward_zero(a * 2^(N-1) / b).
ops.hw_v1: NOT SUPPORTED on v1 (no divider). Device.supported_ops excludes it; the runtime raises SFUnsupportedError. Host pre-flight decides every b == 0 lane before launch.
rewrites: no rewrites; in particular a/b is not a * (1/b) (1/b always overflows)
notes: the event check order is divide first, then overflow; a lane with b == 0 reports divide only
sf.div(where=mask) lowers to a predicated div: masked lanes give 0 and no event

v481.lowering: no SF divide or reciprocal on the chip (ISA s5)

ops.name: fma
ops.semantics: t = mul(a, b) (truncated, may underflow); result = add(t, c) (may saturate). Bit-identical to add(mul(a, b), c). This is NOT a fused single-rounding fma.
rewrites: add(mul(a,b),c) <-> fma(a,b,c) is legal both ways (same bits)
commutative in a and b
notes: on v4.8.1 hardware (wide accumulator, single rounding) this would change: major version bump

v481.lowering: FMA Rd, Ra, Rb with Rd holding c on entry: Rd = c + a*b. Copy c first if it is still needed

ops.name: neg
ops.semantics: -a. Exact (range is symmetric), no events.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1 (ISA section 5): integer ADD x, 0x8000 to flip bit 15, then ACT f=00 with +0 so a 0 input never leaves 0x8000
rewrites: neg(neg(x)) -> x

v481.lowering: ADD n, x, S (flip bit 15), then ACT f=00 Rd, n, Z so a 0 input never leaves 0x8000 (ISA s5)

ops.name: abs
ops.semantics: |a|. Exact, no events.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1 (ISA section 5): abs(x) = ReLU(x) + ReLU(-x), using ACT f=01 for ReLU, neg for -x and ACT f=00 for the add

v481.lowering: abs(x) = ReLU(x) + ReLU(-x): ACT f=01 p, x, Z; ADD n, x, S; ACT f=01 q, n, Z; ACT f=00 Rd, p, q (ISA s5; mind the ACT destination classes)

ops.name: sqrt
ops.semantics: a < 0: invalid, result 0. Else result = isqrt(a * 2^(N-1)) (floor of the exact root). Never overflows.
ops.hw_v1: NOT SUPPORTED on v1 (no sqrt unit); runtime raises SFUnsupportedError

v481.lowering: no sqrt or rsqrt on the chip (ISA s5)

ops.name: widen
ops.semantics: result = a << (M - N). Exact, no events.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: no conversion instruction (ISA section 5). In sign-magnitude it means: magnitude shifted left by M - N, sign bit moved from bit N-1 to bit M-1. Expand or do it on the host

v481.lowering: (derived) free when sfN values are kept left-aligned in 16 bits, as the MX engine expects: the word of an sfN code is already the sf16 word of the same value

ops.name: narrow
ops.semantics: q = round_half_to_even(a / 2^(N-M)) (floor divmod, then round up if remainder > half, or == half and q odd). If |q| > M_max: overflow, clip to +-M_max. underflow if a != 0 and result == 0.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: no conversion instruction; the only hardware rounding is POP on MX results (ISA section 5). Expand or do it on the host
notes: this is the ONLY op that rounds to nearest. All arithmetic truncates toward zero.
on sign-magnitude registers: round the magnitude half to even, then keep the sign. This gives the same result as rounding k, because round half to even is symmetric. A result of 0 must be +0.

v481.lowering: no conversion or rounding instruction on FMA / ACT (ISA s5); the only hardware rounding is POP. Run it on the host, or produce sfN directly from MX with POP at N bits

ops.name: cmp

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne

ops.semantics: Integer compare of the codes (exact).
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1 (ISA section 5): R = ACT f=00 (a, -b), then CMP R, zero. Saturation keeps the sign, so this is exact over the whole range. Only thread 0's NZP steers a branch

mlir.name: sf.cmp (expands to ACT + CMP, not arith.cmpi)

v481.lowering: R = ACT f=00 (a, -b) using ADD n, b, S; then CMP R, Z. Exact over the whole range, because saturation keeps the sign (ISA s5). Like icmp, usable only as a uniform branch condition

ops.name: cmp_lit

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne
attrs.value: int code threshold, decided at trace time

ops.semantics: Compare against a Python literal that may not be representable (e.g. x < 1). The tracer turns the exact literal into an equivalent integer threshold, so the op is a plain integer compare.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: as cmp, with -threshold as a sign-magnitude constant: R = ACT f=00 (a, -t), then CMP R, zero

mlir.name: sf.cmp with a constant (expands to ACT + CMP, not arith.cmpi)

v481.lowering: as cmp, with -threshold built as a sign-magnitude constant: ACT f=00 R, a, (-t); CMP R, Z
v481.cost: 2 instructions plus the constant and the branch

ops.name: maximum
ops.semantics: max of codes. Exact.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: no instruction. Use the exact 16-instruction ReLU sequence in ISA section 5: max(a, b) = max(a+, b+) - min(a-, b-). Do not use b + ReLU(a - b): the difference can saturate

mlir.name: sf.maximum (expands to the ISA ReLU sequence, not arith.maxsi)

rewrites: associative and commutative (legal to reorder)

v481.lowering: the exact 16-instruction sequence of ISA s5: max(a, b) = max(a+, b+) - min(a-, b-). Never b + ReLU(a - b): the difference saturates (wrong on 118 of 1,024 pairs, measured)

ops.name: minimum
ops.semantics: min of codes. Exact.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: no instruction. min(a, b) = -max(-a, -b) with the ISA section 5 sequence, finished as M - P so the result is never -0

mlir.name: sf.minimum (expands to the ISA ReLU sequence, not arith.minsi)

rewrites: associative and commutative

v481.lowering: min(a, b) = -max(-a, -b) with the ISA s5 sequence, finished as M - P so the result is never -0

ops.name: sum
ops.shape: x.shape with axis removed (() for None)
ops.semantics: acc = 0; for i = 0 .. n-1 in index order: acc = add(acc, x[i]) (saturating each step). Overflow if any step saturated. Saturation is sticky in the sense that later steps continue from +-M.
rewrites: NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.
result DEPENDS on order: [M, 1, -1] gives M-1, [1, -1, M] gives M

v481.lowering: an ACT f=00 chain in index order (order matters: it saturates). Across threads (suggested): each thread STRs its value to the scratchpad, then the chain LDRs them in order
v481.cost: 1 ACT per element, plus scratchpad traffic

ops.name: max
ops.semantics: max along axis. Exact.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: tree of the ISA section 5 max sequence
rewrites: any order / tree is legal

v481.lowering: the maximum sequence folded over the elements; any order. Across threads via the scratchpad (suggested)

ops.name: min
ops.semantics: min along axis. Exact.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: tree of the ISA section 5 min sequence
rewrites: any order / tree is legal

v481.lowering: the minimum sequence folded over the elements; any order

ops.name: dot
ops.semantics: For each (i, j): acc = 0; for t = 0 .. k-1: acc = fma(a[i,t], b[t,j], acc). Every product truncated, every add saturated, at width N, in increasing t.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1: a chain of FMA instructions (Rd = accumulator in and out), k in increasing order. Not MX: MX gives different bits (see dot_wide)
rewrites: k must be accumulated in increasing order. Tiling over m and n is free; tiling over k is legal ONLY if the partial sum of tile 1 is fed as the initial acc of tile 2 (no separate partials added later)
split-k, tree reduction, and wider accumulators are NOT legal
notes: sf.addmm(a, b, d) is NOT dot with the accumulator starting at d. It is the dot chain from 0, then ONE saturating add of d: add(dot(a, b), d). The two differ when a partial sum saturates.

v481.lowering: (suggested) per output, an FMA chain in increasing k: FMA acc, a[k], b[k] (LDR the operands first). Never MX: MX gives different bits (ISA s3.4 rule 5)
v481.cost: per output: K FMA plus 2K loads

ops.name: dot_wide

attrs.shift: int from -32 to 31: the result is the total times 2^shift (POP's s)

ops.semantics: The v4.8.1 MX engine. Block: sf9..sf16 use the SF16 block (accumulator W = 25 bits, F = 19 fraction bits); sf4..sf8 use the SF8 block (W = 20, F = 14). Operands are sign-magnitude, left-aligned in 16 bits; am, bm are the magnitudes the block reads (15 bits, or the 7 bits of the top byte on SF8). Product magnitude: SF16 t = (1024 + sum over set bits i of am of ((bm << i) & ~511)) >> 11, so NOT exact; SF8 t = am * bm, exact. Sign = sign(a) xor sign(b). For each (i, j): acc = 0; for k0 = 0, 8, 16, ...: acc = saturate_W(acc + sum of the signed t for k in k0 .. k0+7) (two's complement, about +-32). Result (POP): q = round_half_to_even(|acc| * 2^(shift - F + N - 1)), clamped to M, with the sign of acc; never -0.
ops.hw_v1: v4.8.1 MX engine, one per tile (ISA section 3.4): CFG (block, N) from thread 0, CLR; per chunk of 8 k: WL rows 7..0 then SWAP; MAC per token into slot t (up to 8 tokens per weight tile); then POP with Rs(c) = t << 8 | (shift & 63). 8 output columns per weight tile, 64 MACs per instruction. The engine has no flags.
python: sf.dot(a, b, accumulate="wide", shift=s) in a kernel
a @ b in a kernel traced under sf.accumulate("wide")
sf.matmul / sf.dot / sf.addmm (accumulate="wide") on host and device arrays
rewrites: dot_wide never equals dot: never rewrite one into the other, and never fuse an FMA chain into MX
tiling over m and n is free
tiling over k is legal only by MACing every chunk into the SAME accumulator slot and doing ONE POP at the end; separate POPs added together round twice and are NOT equivalent
chunk boundaries are at k = 0, 8, 16, ... (saturation happens once per chunk); pad a short last chunk with zeros, which add nothing
inside a chunk the order of k does not matter (the 8 products are summed exactly)
notes: overflow means the accumulator clipped at +-32 or the POP result clamped at +-M; underflow means a nonzero acc rounded to 0
on the SF16 block a product below the engine's resolution (e.g. 2^-15 x 2^-15) adds 0, so a total of exactly 0 raises nothing
golden vectors: spec/golden/dot_wide.json, computed by the chip repo's mxref.Engine (sha256 in the file)
the kernel trace picks dot or dot_wide from sf.accumulate at trace time; the kernel cache keys on it

v481.lowering: the MX sequence of ISA s3.4: CFG (block and N, from thread 0) and CLR; per chunk of 8 k: WL rows 7..0 then SWAP; MAC per token into its slot (up to 8 tokens per weight tile); then POP with Rs(c) = slot << 8 | (shift & 63). Thread j supplies lane or column j. 8 output columns per weight tile. Weights are not reset at block start: always load all 8 rows and SWAP
v481.cost: 8 WL + 1 SWAP + 1 MAC per token per chunk of 8 k, then 1 POP per token

ops.name: load
ops.semantics: live = mask AND predicate. Live lanes: ptr[offs]. Others: other. Offsets are element indices, not bytes.
ops.memory: READ global buffer ptr at offs on live lanes only
faults: any live lane with offs < 0 or offs >= buffer size faults the launch. Masked lanes never fault.

v481.lowering: LDR Rd, Ra with Ra a word address below 0xFFC0. Masked lanes: only a tail mask, lowered as the launch's thread count (see the mapping). No bounds check: an out-of-range address silently reads other memory or the scratchpad

ops.name: store
ops.semantics: live = mask AND predicate. ptr[offs] = val on live lanes. If two live lanes hit the same offset, the reference keeps the last lane in row-major order; kernels should not rely on this.
ops.memory: WRITE global buffer ptr at offs on live lanes only
faults: a live lane out of bounds faults the launch. The faulting store writes nothing (no lane, in or out of bounds). Writes by earlier ops stay. See the fault rule.
notes: two programs writing the same address is a race; the result is undefined (the simulator runs programs in order)

v481.lowering: STR Ra, Rv (address register first). Same mask and bounds rules as load. If several threads store to one address in one instruction, the highest thread's value lands last (derived)
v481.cost: about 10 + 8 x 16 cycles for 8 threads (2 beats each)

ops.name: shared_load

attrs.buf: shared buffer id (declared on the kernel)

ops.semantics: Live lanes read shared[buf][idx]; masked lanes give 0.
faults: live lane out of bounds faults

v481.lowering: LDR from 0xFFC0 + index. At most 64 words per tile. The scratchpad is NEVER cleared, but DSL shared memory starts at 0: emit the zeroing stores if the kernel reads before writing

ops.name: shared_store
ops.semantics: Live lanes write shared[buf][idx] = val.
ops.memory: WRITE block-local shared buffer. Shared memory is zeroed at the start of every program.
faults: live lane out of bounds faults

v481.lowering: STR to 0xFFC0 + index; at most 64 words per tile

ops.name: barrier
ops.semantics: All lanes of the block reach this point before any continues. In lockstep IR this orders shared-memory accesses; nothing may be moved across it.
notes: must not be placed under a divergent predicate

v481.lowering: nothing to emit inside a block: every instruction finishes for all 8 threads before the next, so a store is visible to the whole block from the next instruction (ISA s1.5). There is no barrier between blocks

A block of L lanes (@sf.jit vector, @sf.kernel block)
8 hardware threads. L <= 8: one lane per thread, the rest disabled. L > 8 (suggested): each thread handles lanes j, j+8, j+16, ... in sequence (strip-mining)
No argument registers. Lower to LDR from a parameter block at a fixed data address, indexed by R13 if per block (GPT-2 puts a 4-word block table at word 0)
16-bit word addresses: offsets are already element indices, one word per sf16 value. Buffers must lie in 0x0000..0xFFBF, and a range compared with CMP must not cross 0x8000 (CMP is signed)
16-bit sign-magnitude words, sfN left-aligned; 0x8000 reads as 0 and results never produce it. No conversion on load or store
i16, wrapping. Keep every int in -32768..32767
Cannot be stored: nothing writes a comparison to a register. A condition exists only as NZP after CMP, and only thread 0's steers a branch
No predication. A tail mask offs < n lowers to launching exactly n threads, so the spare threads are disabled and touch no memory. Any other mask has no lowering
No predication. Only SF values can be if-converted, arithmetically with ReLU (ISA s5); everything else must be uniform
The SF IR is straight-line: Python loops are unrolled when a kernel is traced. With 512 program words the compiler must re-roll loops into BR loops (uniform trip counts only)
Emit CMP R0, R0 first so an unconditional BRnzp is taken; end every path with RET
The chip has no flags, so the compiler emits nothing for them. The host gets counts by replay (sf.config(status="replay"))
13 registers. Spill to the scratchpad, 8 words per thread at 0xFFC0 + 8*tid + k

gaps: Blocks bigger than 8 lanes: strip-mine (mapping table).
Integers wider than 16 bits: unsupported on the chip.
Divergent control flow and general masks: not lowerable; only tail masks and SF if-conversion.
and, or, xor, not, bool_to_int, iabs: no lowering.
General integer division and modulo: only the ISA's constant divisors.
div, sqrt (and exp, log, softmax, LayerNorm and similar in models): host only.

narrow: no conversion instruction. Note that the width rule (sfN on the sf16 path, re-truncated after every op) needs masking, and v4.8.1 has no AND, so sfN below 16 is best done through MX, where N is a CFG setting.
Faults: the DSL faults on out-of-bounds; the chip has no bounds checks at all.
